Essential ingredients

examples.title: Example 1 — simple (teaching example)
examples.body: A short everyday fact pattern is tested against “Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc”. Name BNS s. 326, list the ingredients, and say which facts match. This is a teaching example — the statute does not print a numbered illustration under this heading.

examples.title: Example 2 — practical application / distinction (teaching example)
examples.body: Change one ingredient so that BNS s. 326 fails. A complex problem or motion often hinges on this subtle missing ingredient. State the failure expressly. Label this as an example, never as a reported case.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 326 (Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.

misconceptions.trap: Writing only the section number and title without analyzing ingredients or case ratio.
misconceptions.correction: An authoritative note defines the concept, lists ingredients, uses an illustration, states explanations/exceptions, applies the test, and concludes with BNS s. 326.

misconceptions.trap: Copying a statutory illustration without mapping it to an ingredient.
misconceptions.correction: Quote the illustration, then write which ingredient it proves or which ingredient is missing. Mapping is the core evidentiary link.

misconceptions.trap: Giving a one-line summary or shortened explanation of the provision.
misconceptions.correction: Authoritative chamber practice and judicial papers require a complete answer. The analysis on this page is written at full length for that reason.

examTips: Cite BNS s. 326 for offences on or after 1 July 2024.
Ingredients first, illustration second, application third, conclusion last.
Do not cite the IPC number in a post-1 July 2024 charge-sheet unless s. 358 savings apply.

examFrameworks.question: Structured Legal Assessment: BNS s. 326 (Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc).
steps: Introduce BNS s. 326 and Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property.
Define / state the meaning in your own words.
Give one labelled example and map it to an ingredient.
Apply in four to six sentences.
Conclude with the current citation — BNS s. 326.

examFrameworks.question: Comprehensive Chamber Written Submissions: BNS s. 326 with connected statutory scheme.
steps: Everything in the preliminary assessment, written in full substantive depth — not summarised.
Place the section in the Chapter and explain why the heading exists.
Work a second hypothetical in which one ingredient fails.
Add analytical comment on a condition or practical difficulty.
IRAC application to the problem facts.
Address procedural hurdles, evidentiary requirements, and standard defense objections.

answerSkeleton: Introduction — BNS s. 326, Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc.
revisionPoints: BNS s. 326: Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc.
First ingredient: Whoever commits mischief by,
No printed illustration — prepare an original labelled example.

For offences on or after 1 July 2024, the correct citation is BNS s. 326 — Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc. Older books and judgments may still print a historical number (435 / 436). Convert it. Write the BNS number in a current answer. Do not treat the old number as if it were still the law.
